newsitem.title: USA: CME hogs end mixed while pork bellies close weaker.
newsitem.headline: CME hogs end mixed while pork bellies close weaker.

text.p: CME hog futures recovered late and turned mixed by the close with July and August again setting new contract highs. February pork bellies remained weak at the close on concern over Tuesday's storage report.
Hogs closed 0.500 cent higher to 0.500 lower with February off 0.200 at 78.675 cents. July posted a new high of 77.225 and August 73.925 cents by the close.

Hog futures rallied on renewed concern over the forecast for bitter cold weather by the weekend. Continued bullish ideas from the last Hogs and Pigs report added to stength in summer months, traders said.

Futures had been under pressure early from a weaker than expected tone to cash hogs and sliding pork cutout values. Expectations had been for cash markets to hold around steady in the face of cold weather but the lowest pork cutout value since late April and adequate marketings kept packer bids down, they said.

However, selling lacked follow through and prices drifted back up despite losses in other meat pits. Expectations are that hog runs will still lighten later in the week as even colder temperatures move into the Midwest, they said.
